sentences.sentence: The NHS says feeling sick is common and usually goes away on its own.

sentences.sentence: Diarrhoea or vomiting can point to norovirus or food poisoning, and a headache with a high temperature can suggest an infection such as flu.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages). | second pass: supported

sentences.sentence: Other causes include morning sickness in pregnancy, motion sickness, anxiety, alcohol, medicines and recent surgery.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages). | second pass: supported

sentences.sentence: NHS inform calls gastroenteritis one of the most common causes of vomiting in adults, and also lists migraine, labyrinthitis, appendicitis and medicines such as antibiotics and opioid painkillers.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages). | second pass: supported

sentences.sentence: NHS inform says norovirus usually clears up by itself within a few days, and that there is no specific treatment, so the illness has to run its course.
sentences.note: Edited after second pass: Retrieved text for this is from NHS inform's Norovirus page (usually clears in a few days, no specific treatment, run its course), not from NHS trust leaflets; no trust leaflet text was retrieved. Attribution overstated.

sentences.sentence: NHS inform says antibiotics will not help norovirus because it is caused by a virus, and that small sips of water help to prevent dehydration.
sentences.note: Edited after second pass: Retrieved text attributes antibiotics not working (norovirus is a virus) to NHS inform's norovirus page, and sipping water to prevent dehydration to NHS inform's vomiting page; no trust-leaflet text retrieved.

sentences.sentence: The NHS describes getting fresh air, sipping cold drinks, trying ginger or peppermint tea, and eating smaller, more frequent meals.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages). | second pass: supported

sentences.sentence: It also lists hot, fried or greasy food, eating too quickly and lying down soon after eating as things to avoid.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages). | second pass: supported

sentences.sentence: NHS inform advises resting at home and taking small sips of water or squash often so that dehydration does not develop.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages). | second pass: supported

sentences.sentence: NHS inform lists signs of severe dehydration, including confusion, a rapid heartbeat, sunken eyes and passing little or no urine, among the reasons to call NHS 111.
sentences.note: Edited after second pass: On NHS inform's vomiting page these signs (confusion, rapid heartbeat, sunken eyes, little or no urine) are listed as signs of SEVERE dehydration under the call-111 advice, not as general warning signs; the gastroenteritis page puts confusion under 999/A&E and little urine with dizziness under urgen

sentences.sentence: NHS inform advises people with diabetes who have been vomiting a lot to call NHS 111, especially if they take insulin, because vomiting can affect blood sugar levels.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages). | second pass: supported

sentences.sentence: NHS inform says to call 999 or go to A&E for vomit that contains blood or looks like coffee granules, or for green or yellow-green vomit.
sentences.note: Edited after second pass: NHS inform says blood in vomit or coffee-granule vomit, and green or yellow-green vomit, mean call 999 or go to A&E; the sentence says only 'the NHS' and 'A&E', dropping 999 and misnaming the publisher.

sentences.sentence: NHS inform advises calling NHS 111 for a person who keeps being sick and cannot keep fluids down, has been vomiting for more than 2 days, or has lost a lot of weight since becoming ill; its gastroenteritis page lists fever and bloody diarrhoea as reasons to contact NHS 111 or the GP practice urgently.
sentences.note: Edited after second pass: Vomiting page supports: can't keep fluids down, vomiting more than 2 days, lost a lot of weight. Fever and bloody diarrhoea came from the gastroenteritis page (fever over 38C or bloody diarrhoea: contact 111 or the GP urgently), so single-page attribution is wrong and the GP route is omitted.

sentences.sentence: The NHS says to call 999 if sudden sickness comes with tight or heavy chest pain, pain spreading to the arms, back, neck or jaw, or shortness of breath, because these could be signs of a heart attack.

sentences.sentence: The NHS advises seeing a GP if the sickness has not improved after a few days or keeps coming back, and calling NHS 111 for advice if a GP cannot be seen.

sentences.sentence: The GP can look for the cause and may prescribe anti-sickness medicine.
